actions.action: Calculate all six totals from stated usage
actions.mechanism: Shared usage inputs expose required add-ons before selection rather than presenting base prices as payable totals.
actions.implementation: Ask for storage, editors, guests, and export needs. Recalculate every plan with required charges and explicitly selected options; show billing period and amount due.
actions.check: Run usage fixtures across requirement thresholds; verify displayed totals against structured charges for all six plans.
actions.risk: Unanswered usage inputs must produce labeled estimates, not definitive totals.

actions.action: Separate required charges from optional choices
actions.mechanism: Explicit charge categories distinguish unavoidable costs, usage-triggered requirements, and genuinely discretionary purchases without relying on color.
actions.implementation: Label line items “Included,” “Required for your usage,” or “Optional—not selected.” Explain requirement triggers; leave discretionary options unchecked.
actions.check: Ask visitors which charges they can decline without losing their stated requirements; compare answers with charge rules.
actions.risk: A conditionally required add-on must not retain an optional label.

actions.action: Keep a complete, accessible comparison matrix
actions.mechanism: Consistent rows expose capability differences even when a plan cannot satisfy the visitor’s stated usage.
actions.implementation: Show all six plans with storage, editors, guests, exports, charges, and totals. Use semantic headers and explicit “Unavailable” or “Limit exceeded” text.
actions.check: Using a screen reader, locate each plan’s export limit and unavailable capabilities; verify header associations and keyboard access.
actions.risk: Never imply that purchasing an add-on resolves an unsupported capability.

actions.action: Explain what changed each plan’s total
actions.mechanism: A traceable cost breakdown connects usage requirements to charges, making superficially similar base prices distinguishable.
actions.implementation: Under each total, show base charge, required add-ons, selected options, quantities, and arithmetic. Attach the triggering usage rule to each required item.
actions.check: Choose a plan with a required add-on; verify a visitor can explain its total using visible quantities and charges.
actions.risk: Dense breakdowns need concise summaries without concealing mandatory charges.

actions.mechanism: Boundary previews reveal when a small usage change activates another charge or exceeds a hard capability limit.
actions.implementation: From structured rules, show the next relevant threshold for each plan and its cost consequence. Offer keyboard-operable usage adjustments without changing the original scenario silently.
actions.check: Test immediately below, at, and above each threshold; verify charges, unavailability messages, and announced total updates.
actions.risk: Do not present hypothetical growth as predicted visitor behavior.

actions.action: Carry the compared configuration into checkout
actions.mechanism: A shared quote prevents checkout from introducing requirements absent from the comparison the visitor used.
actions.implementation: Persist usage, selected options, required charges, and pricing version. Before payment, show the same breakdown; require review if configuration or pricing changes.
actions.check: Compare comparison-page and checkout line items for identical scenarios; inject a version change and verify explicit review.
actions.risk: A review checkbox alone does not establish understanding.

actions.mechanism: Rule validation catches missing dependencies and contradictory classifications before they can generate misleading plan totals.
actions.implementation: Validate all six plans for charge identifiers, billing units, requirement predicates, dependency cycles, and capability limits. Block publication on unresolved required-charge references.
actions.check: Inject missing add-ons, cyclic dependencies, and incompatible billing units; verify validation rejects each fixture with a specific error.
actions.risk: Schema validity alone cannot establish that business rules are correct.

actions.action: Test comprehension with two similar plans
actions.mechanism: A task-based comparison measures whether visitors understand payable totals and distinguish required purchases from optional extras.
actions.implementation: Within the six-plan page, test two similar base-price plans: one requires an add-on for the scenario; the other includes that capability.
actions.check: Ask participants to identify both totals, explain their difference, and name declinable extras. Record errors, including screen-reader sessions.
actions.risk: Correct plan selection without a correct explanation can mask guessing.
